topic: Scourge progression gated by purchased Memories
currentUserGoal: Make the first playthrough die extremely quickly and require actual skill or Memory investment, rather than repeated losses, to earn longer runs.
workCompleted: Identified that the prototype was granting an exponential Scourge-ramp slowdown from completedRuns, so merely losing repeatedly made later runs dramatically easier.
Removed completed-run count from Scourge pacing and keyed the breathing-room curve to the number of unlocked production-chain helper Memories instead.
Preserved the intended three-second fresh failure and the multi-minute Tiny Sprinkler follow-up band.
Added a regression proving that an unupgraded save with twelve completed losses still dies in the same brief onboarding window as Run 1.
Verified a genuinely fresh Run 1 on an isolated localhost browser origin without touching the user's 127.0.0.1 prototype save.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 126 Vitest tests across 17 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
The focused EcosystemSystem suite passed 17 tests.
An isolated browser save reached Game Over on Run 1 at exactly 3000 ms.
The fresh browser run remained at 144 FPS with zero frame spikes and no browser errors or warnings.
The deterministic second-run Tiny Sprinkler simulation remains inside its intended 150-330 second band.

release.status: Local ecosystem prototype checkpoint; not pushed, merged into master, or promoted to production.

currentGitStatus: The Scourge Memory-gating correction, regression test, and handoff are committed together on codex/ecosystem-factory-prototype.
docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md remains an unrelated untracked file and must stay untouched unless the user explicitly requests it.
The local Vite server remains available at http://127.0.0.1:5173.
knownIssues: A save with unlocked helper Memories intentionally receives a longer Scourge ramp because that is now earned permanent progression.
Numeric helper ranks currently extend survival through their production effects rather than directly slowing Scourge demand.
The HUD shows the run number but does not yet explicitly label the helper-Memory tier that controls the opening demand ramp.
nextRecommendedSteps: Have the user begin another run on their existing save and judge whether its duration matches the Memories they have actually purchased.
Tune the first Tiny Sprinkler purchase race after hands-on testing without weakening the unupgraded three-second failure.
Continue the visible Field Mouse resource-chain objective once the opening progression feels correct.
doNotRevert: Do not use completedRuns to grant Scourge relief; run count is history, not power.
Keep the unupgraded first-run and repeated-loss duration regression bands at 2-4 seconds unless the user explicitly changes the target.
Keep the first-loss GT guarantee so the Tiny Sprinkler unlock remains immediately affordable.
Keep later survival grounded in unlocked production Memories, run-local equipment, and Care throughput.
